book.subtitle: A CEFR A2 Educational Adaptation of George Orwell
book.author: George Orwell

week.title: The Note

chapter_opening.intro: Winston thinks the dark-haired woman may be watching him. He believes she could work for the Thought Police. Then, one day, she falls near him in a corridor. Winston helps her. For one second, their hands touch. She puts something small into his hand. Later, Winston opens it. There are only three words: I LOVE YOU.
chapter_opening.alt_text: Winston bends down to help Julia in a cold Ministry corridor while Party workers pass nearby. She secretly places a small folded note into his hand under surveillance cameras.

paragraphs: For several days, Winston cannot stop thinking about the dark-haired woman.
He sees her sometimes at the Ministry of Truth.
Why does she appear near him so often?
Did she follow him to Mr. Charrington's shop?
Does she know about the diary?
Does she work for the Thought Police?
And in Oceania, not knowing is dangerous.
One day, Winston walks through a corridor at the Ministry.
The dark-haired woman is ahead of him.
Her arm is already injured, and the fall hurts her.
The moment lasts only a second.
His heart begins to beat faster.
He puts the paper into his pocket.
For the next few minutes, Winston can think about nothing else.
Maybe the note says: I know what you are doing.
Maybe it is from the Thought Police.
He wants to read it immediately.
Finally, when nobody is looking directly at him, he opens the paper.
For a moment, he cannot think.
This is not what he expected.
The woman does not want to arrest him.
Or at least Winston hopes that is true.
Now Winston has a new problem.
How can he speak to her?
Party members are watched at work.
They are watched in public places.
Even a long conversation can look suspicious.
For several days, Winston tries to get close to her.
Sometimes too many people are nearby.
Sometimes she is surrounded by coworkers.
Sometimes a telescreen is directly above them.
Finally, he sees her alone in the canteen.
They do not look directly at each other.
They cannot stay together for long.
They will meet in a crowded public square.
A large crowd can sometimes hide two people better than an empty room.
Later, Winston arrives at the square.
A group of prisoners is passing through.
They stand next to each other.
They do not look like lovers.
They do not even look like friends.
Their hands touch for a moment inside the crowd.
On the day of the meeting, Winston travels out of London.
For the first time in a long time, Winston hears natural sounds.
She leads him through the trees.
They do not speak much at first.
Finally, they reach a quiet place.
Julia explains that she hates the Party.
She knows how to look loyal.
She follows rules when people are watching.
But she does not believe in the Party.
He thought she was one of the most loyal people he knew.
It keeps people from asking questions.
But Julia is different from him.
He wants to understand how the Party controls everything.
Julia is less interested in these questions.
She hates the Party because it tries to control her life.
For Winston, it is also political.
They cannot use the same place too often.
They need to plan every movement.
For years, he believed nobody understood what he felt.
Now there is another person who also hates the Party.
Eventually, Winston thinks about Mr. Charrington's room.
Winston knows renting it is dangerous.
But he wants a private place.
He and Julia begin using the room.
For a short time, it feels like another world.
The room smells different from Party buildings.
Outside, people live their ordinary lives.
Inside, Winston and Julia can talk.
They do not need to perform for the Party.
She brings bread that is better than Party food.
Sometimes she has small things that are difficult to find.
Winston asks where she gets them.
She knows how the system works.
She breaks rules without speaking about revolution all the time.
One afternoon, Julia sees the glass paperweight.
Winston explains that it is old.
The small piece of coral is protected inside the glass.
To Winston, it feels like their secret life.
He imagines that he and Julia are inside the glass too.
But Winston knows they are not really safe.
He tells Julia: We are already dead.
He means that one day the Party will discover them.
Julia does not want to think about that day.
She wants to enjoy the time they have.
Winston cannot stop thinking about the future.
Still, he continues returning to the room.
For the first time in years, Winston experiences something like happiness.
He has someone to speak to.
Someone who understands what it means to hate the Party.
The room becomes important to him.
For a short time, Winston believes a private world can exist.
A world where Big Brother cannot enter.

secondary_illustration.alt_text: Winston and Julia sit close together in the warm room above Mr. Charrington's shop. The glass paperweight with coral rests on the table beside them, creating a brief sense of privacy and safety.

end_of_chapter: Winston once believed Julia might be his enemy.
Now she is the person he trusts most.
The Party wants loyalty to Big Brother.
Winston gives his loyalty to another person.
But the room above the shop feels safe.
And Winston wants to believe that feeling.

quick_check.question: What does Julia secretly give Winston?
Why can't Winston read the note immediately?
options: There are people and telescreens around him.
Julia tells him to wait one week.
The note is written in Newspeak.
quick_check.answer: There are people and telescreens around him.

quick_check.question: Where do Winston and Julia first plan a private meeting?
Julia is completely loyal to the Party.
Winston and Julia rebel against the Party in exactly the same way.
Why do Winston and Julia use the room above Mr. Charrington's shop?
options: It is close to Winston's office.
It appears to have no telescreen.
O'Brien told them to use it.
quick_check.answer: It appears to have no telescreen.

quick_check.question: What does the paperweight begin to represent?

example: First, Julia gives Winston a note.
Later, they meet outside the city.
Finally, they begin using the room above the shop.

order_items.event: Winston and Julia use the room above the shop.

questions.question: Julia give / gave Winston a note.
Winston read / reads the message later.
They meet / met outside the city.
Julia tell / told Winston her name.
Winston begin / began to trust Julia.

orwells_question.question: Why is Winston and Julia's relationship dangerous to the Party?
options: Because Julia does not work hard enough.
Because private loyalty can become stronger than loyalty to the Party.
Because Winston wants a different apartment.
orwells_question.preferred_answer: Because private loyalty can become stronger than loyalty to the Party.
orwells_question.feedback: The Party wants people to direct their deepest loyalty toward Big Brother. Winston and Julia create something the Party cannot completely control: a private relationship.

second_reflection.question: Winston and Julia both hate the Party. But why are they different?
options: Winston thinks more about truth and history; Julia focuses more on personal freedom.
Julia loves Big Brother but Winston does not.
There is no difference between them.
second_reflection.preferred_answer: Winston thinks more about truth and history; Julia focuses more on personal freedom.
second_reflection.feedback: Two people can resist the same system for different reasons. Winston wants to understand the Party. Julia mainly wants the Party to leave her private life alone.

speaking.question: Which is more dangerous to a system like the Party: a political rebellion or a private relationship?

writing.prompt: Winston believes the room above the shop is safe. Would you trust this place? Why or why not?

learning_outcomes: Understand why Winston initially fears Julia.
Understand how Julia gives Winston the note.
Explain why communication is difficult under surveillance.
Understand how Winston and Julia meet.
Compare Winston and Julia's ideas about rebellion.
Explain why the room above the shop matters.
Understand what the paperweight begins to symbolize.
Explain why private relationships are dangerous to the Party.

next_week.teaser: Winston believes O'Brien may also hate the Party. Then O'Brien finally gives him a reason to visit. For Winston, this may be the beginning of resistance — or something much worse.

implementation_notes.primary_goal: Story first. Learning around the story, not in the way of the story.
reading_rules: Do not interrupt the story with mandatory exercises.
Allow the learner to read the full chapter before showing required questions.
Short page breaks or scene breaks are allowed for readability, but they must not insert tasks between story sections.
The secondary illustration may appear inside the story as visual support only, with no blocking question attached.
interaction_rules: Quick Check, Language Check, Orwell's Question and Second Reflection appear only after End of Chapter.
Orwell's Question and Second Reflection must be multiple-choice or choice-based, not open writing.
Speaking and Writing are optional classroom activities and must never block progress.
Vocabulary should work best as tap-to-open cards, popovers or lightweight glossary support.
ui_tone: Weeks 1–2 are cold and oppressive. Week 3 may become warmer and more intimate inside the room, but should still feel fragile and unsafe.
Use restrained red accents and warm amber only in the secret room scenes.
